leaf.question: Can a provider-independent expected-version state machine prove same-intent duplicate-commit safety without relying on an undocumented same-path create-if-absent guarantee?
leaf.candidate: atomic expected-version compare-and-swap state transition with durable intent membership

formal_model.state: S=(version, committed), where version is a monotone integer and committed is a map intent_id -> effect_digest.
formal_model.required_primitive: CAS(expected_version, replacement_state) is atomic: it succeeds iff the durable state's current version equals expected_version, otherwise it performs no write and returns conflict.
formal_model.proposal: An actor reads S=(v,C). If intent_id is already in C, it returns ALREADY_COMMITTED with no mutation. Otherwise it constructs S'=(v+1, C union {intent_id:effect_digest}) and attempts CAS(v,S').
formal_model.success_rule: Only a successful CAS is a logical commit. A failed CAS has zero durable effect and requires a later invocation/fresh read rather than same-run waiting or retry.
formal_model.scope_guard: The logical effect tested here is the durable committed-map transition itself. This model does not prove exactly-once execution of an arbitrary non-transactional external side effect.

deterministic_two_actor_interleaving.class: same intent, same base version, A-CAS-before-B-CAS
trace: A reads S0=(7,{}) and prepares S1=(8,{I:E}).
B reads the same S0=(7,{}) and prepares the same logical replacement S1=(8,{I:E}).
A executes CAS(7,S1); current version is 7, so A succeeds and durable state becomes S1.
B executes CAS(7,S1); current version is now 8, so B conflicts and performs no durable write.
A later acknowledgement is irrelevant to uniqueness: durable committed membership for I exists exactly once.
On a later fresh invocation, B reads S1, observes I in committed, and returns ALREADY_COMMITTED without mutation.
deterministic_two_actor_interleaving.invariant: For intent I, cardinality of successful logical commits is <= 1.
deterministic_two_actor_interleaving.proof: Both actors can commit only via CAS from version 7. Atomic expected-version CAS permits at most one success from a single durable version. The first success increments the version to 8; every remaining CAS carrying expected_version=7 has zero effect. Because committed[I] is inserted in the same atomic replacement as the version increment, a later fresh reader deterministically suppresses a duplicate same-intent commit.

leaf.semantic_conclusion: The r253 provider-specific same-path-create gap can be avoided at the formal coordination layer by requiring an explicit atomic expected-version primitive rather than inferring create-if-absent linearizability. The tested interleaving has at-most-one logical commit. This is a provider-independent architecture condition, not evidence that any particular repository API supplies the primitive, and it does not establish exactly-once arbitrary external effects.
